'''James Mitchell Tour''' is an American [[chemist]] and [[nanotechnologist]]. He is T. T. and W. F. Chao Professor of Chemistry at [[Rice University]], and a joint professor of [[materials science]] and [[nanoengineering]].<ref name="Rice Profile2">{{cite web |title=James Tour |url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/james-tour |website=[[Rice University]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260818110005/https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/james-tour |archive-date=18 August 2026 |url-status=live}}</ref> He is a proponent and advocate of [[intelligent design]], a [[Pseudoscience|pseudoscientific]] [[Creationism|creationist]] argument for the [[existence of God]], and is a skeptic of [[origin of life]] research.

== Education ==
Tour graduated from [[Syracuse University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in chemistry in 1981. He then earned his [[Ph.D.]] in [[synthetic chemistry]] and [[organometallic chemistry]] from [[Purdue University]] in 1986 under Nobel laureate [[Ei-ichi Negishi]]. After receiving his doctorate, he completed postdoctoral research at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] (1986–1987) and [[Stanford University]] (1987–1988).<ref>{{Cite web |title=James M. Tour |url=https://jmtour.com/resume-dr-james-tour/ |website=James Tour Group}}</ref>

== Career ==
Tour and colleagues worked on [[materials science]], specifically on the use of [[graphene]] as a scaffolding gel, as reported by [[The New Yorker]].<ref name="Colapinto" />

Tour has also been involved in scientific outreach, such as [[nanoputian|NanoKids]], an interactive learning DVD to teach children fundamentals of chemistry and [[physics]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Rovner |first1=Sophie L. |last2=C |last3=Washington |first3=En |date=January 21, 2025 |title='Nanokids' Try to Get into Middle School |url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/82/i14/NANOKIDSTRY-MIDDLE-SCHOOL.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=January 2, 2026 |website=Chemical & Engineering News |language=en |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> He has testified before the US Congress on two occasions to warn about budget cuts.<ref name="Colapinto">{{Cite magazine |last=Colapinto |first=John |author-link=John Colapinto |title=Material Question |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2014/12/22/material-question |access-date=December 11, 2020 |magazine=[[The New Yorker]] |date=December 14, 2014 |language=en-us |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

In the ''[[Scientific American]]'' article "Better Killing Through Chemistry", which appeared a few months after the [[September 11 attacks]], Tour highlighted the ease of obtaining [[chemical weapon]] precursors in the [[United States]].<ref>{{cite journal |last=Musser |first=George |date=November 2001 |title=Better Killing through Chemistry: Buying chemical weapons material through the mail is quick and easy |journal=[[Scientific American]] |volume=285 |issue=6 |pages=20–21 |url=http://www.sciam.com/article.cfm?articleID=000E51F9-AA56-1C75-9B81809EC588EF21 |access-date=September 6, 2007 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican1201-20 |pmid=11759580 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

In 2002, he was the head of the molecular electronics group at the Center for Nanoscale Science and Technology at [[Rice University]].<ref>{{cite encyclopedia |last=Freitas |first=Robert A. |date=2002 |title=Nanotecnologie |language=it |trans-title=Nanotechnology |url=https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/nanotecnologie_(Il-Libro-dell'Anno)/ |encyclopedia=Il Libro dell'Anno 2002 |publisher=[[Treccani]] |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

==Religion and evolution==
Tour became a [[born-again Christian]] as an undergraduate, and in 2001 he signed the [[Discovery Institute]]'s ''[[A Scientific Dissent from Darwinism]]'' statement that relies on [[pseudoscientific]] reasoning to offer various [[objections to evolution|religiously motivated arguments against evolution]].<ref name="chang">{{cite news |last1=Chang |first1=Kenneth |date=February 21, 2006 |title=Few Biologists but Many Evangelicals Sign Anti-Evolution Petition |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2006/02/21/science/sciencespecial2/few-biologists-but-many-evangelicals-sign.html |access-date=August 17, 2026 |work=[[The New York Times]] |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> In a 2014 profile in ''[[The New Yorker]]'', Tour was reported to have indicated that this signing "reflected only his personal doubts about how random mutation occurs at the molecular level. Although he ends e-mails with 'God bless', he says that, apart from a habit of praying for divine guidance, he feels that religion plays no part in his scientific work."<ref name="Colapinto" /> Tour has subsequently become more outspoken about his scepticism regarding [[origin of life]] research, including in a debate with science YouTuber [[Dave Farina]] at a May 2023 event at Rice University.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shad |first=Nayeli |date=May 2023 |title=Rice's James Tour and YouTuber 'Professor Dave' debate the origins of life |url=https://www.ricethresher.org/article/2023/05/rices-james-tour-and-youtuber-professor-dave-debate-the-origins-of-life |access-date=March 17, 2025 |website=The Rice Thresher |language=en-US |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>

Tour is a member of Discovery Institute,<ref>{{Cite web |title=James Tour |url=https://www.discovery.org/p/tour/ |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=Discovery Institute |language=en-US |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref> and has worked with [[Stephen C. Meyer]] to promote [[intelligent design]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Extravagant Claims: James Tour & Stephen Meyer Critique Origin of Life Research |date= |url=https://www.discovery.org/podcast/extravagant-claims-james-tour-stephen-meyer-critique-origin-of-life-research/ |website=[[Discovery Institute]] |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Beyond Evolution: Unraveling the Origins of Life with Stephen Meyer and James Tour |date=August 5, 2024 |url=https://www.hoover.org/research/beyond-evolution-unraveling-origins-life-stephen-meyer-and-james-tour |website=[[Hoover Institute]] |archive-url= |archive-date=}}</ref>
